item.title: A foreigner on a mandate contract or B2B - what happens to the work permit after a change of contract [COSC own material]
item.description:
The Act of 11 March 2026 (Dz.U. 2026 poz. 473) added art. 33 ust. 2 pkt 3 and art. 69 pkt 5 to the Act of 20 March 2025 (Dz.U. 2025 poz. 621). Concluding an employment contract instead of a civil law contract - voluntarily or in execution of a PIP decision under art. 11 ust. 1 pkt 7a - does not require a new work permit or a new entry of the declaration in the register. The exclusion does not cover a change of employer, a change of position or a change of residence title; under a single permit for residence and work the type of contract is part of the decision (art. 118 ust. 1 pkt 5 of the Act on Foreigners) and it is changed under art. 120.
Source: Centrum Obsługi Spraw Cudzoziemców (materiał własny) More & contact: https://cosc.org.pl/artykul-cudzoziemiec-zlecenie-b2b-reklasyfikacja-zezwolenie.html?lang=en&utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=aktualnosci-en • WhatsApp +48 539 999 549

item.title: EES has replaced passport stamps - fewer forgeries at the border
item.description:
The Border Guard (Straz Graniczna) reports that after the full launch of the Entry/Exit System (EES) in April 2026 the stamping of passports of foreigners covered by that procedure was discontinued, and entries and exits are recorded electronically. The result is a clear fall in the number of forged border control stamps. Attempts are still detected: on 29 August 2026 at the Medyka crossing four forged Hungarian stamps were found in the passport of a 41 year old Ukrainian national; she voluntarily accepted a penalty of 6 months' imprisonment suspended for one year. For foreigners this means that time spent in the Schengen area is now counted from the electronic register, not from stamps in the document, and attempting to 'correct' entry history is both ineffective and punishable.
Source: Straż Graniczna More & contact: https://cosc.org.pl/aktualnosci.html?lang=en&utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=aktualnosci-en • WhatsApp +48 539 999 549

item.title: Labour inspector's order concerning a civil-law contract [own material, COSC]
item.description:
Own material of the Centre for Foreigners' Affairs Service (Centrum Obslugi Spraw Cudzoziemcow). The Act of 11 March 2026 (Dz.U. 2026 poz. 473) does not allow the labour inspectorate to reclassify a civil-law contract straight away. First an order to remove infringements is issued under art. 11 ust. 2 of the Act on the National Labour Inspectorate (Państwowa Inspekcja Pracy, PIP) - after the parties have been given the opportunity to state their position, in writing, with a deadline set so that compliance can be assessed during the inspection (art. 34 ust. 1c). Only failure to comply opens the way to a decision under art. 11 ust. 1 pkt 7a. We also explain why a foreigner moving from a mandate contract or a B2B arrangement to an employment contract does not require a new work permit or a new entry of the declaration in the register (art. 33 ust. 2 pkt 3 and art. 69 pkt 5 of the Act of 20 March 2025).

item.title: Labour inspectorate decision establishing an employment relationship [own material, COSC]
item.description:
Own material of the Centre for Foreigners' Affairs Service (Centrum Obslugi Spraw Cudzoziemcow). From 8 July 2026 the regional labour inspector may establish the existence of an employment relationship by way of a decision (art. 11 ust. 1 pkt 7a of the Act on the National Labour Inspectorate, Państwowa Inspekcja Pracy, PIP; Dz.U. 2026 poz. 473). The decision may only be issued where an earlier order to remove infringements has not been complied with. We discuss the course of the proceedings under art. 33a, the mandatory content of the decision, the default rules applied where evidence is missing (contract for an indefinite period, full-time work, minimum remuneration), the date the contract is deemed concluded, and the effects under labour, tax and social insurance law.

item.title: Checks on app drivers near Chopin Airport: five foreigners banned from re-entry
item.description:
The Border Guard (Straż Graniczna) and the Warsaw Metropolitan Police Headquarters checked, as part of the "Bezpieczny Przewóz" (Safe Transport) operation, the residence legality of drivers providing passenger transport through mobile apps around Warsaw Chopin Airport. Five foreigners were detained: two citizens of Uzbekistan and one each from Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Georgia. Four were using annulled or temporarily invalid Latvian and Bulgarian visas and had nonetheless filed applications for temporary residence permits with the voivodes while staying in Poland unlawfully. Return proceedings were opened against all of them; in three cases decisions were issued with a ban on re-entering Poland and the other Schengen states for 18 months to 3 years. The case shows that merely filing a residence application does not cure earlier unlawful residence and does not confer the right to work.
Source: Straż Graniczna More & contact: https://cosc.org.pl/aktualnosci.html?lang=en&utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=aktualnosci-en • WhatsApp +48 539 999 549

item.title: Online transmission during a PIP (Panstwowa Inspekcja Pracy - National Labour Inspectorate) inspection - when the inspector may demand it [COSC own material]
item.description:
The Act of 11 March 2026 (Dz.U. 2026 poz. 473) added art. 23 ust. 1 pkt 2a to the Act on the PIP (Panstwowa Inspekcja Pracy - National Labour Inspectorate). A labour inspector may demand an online transmission enabling inspection of documents, hearing of the party and questioning of the inspected entity - in justified cases and where this does not conflict with the purpose of the inspection. We explain the limits of such a demand, the data minimisation principle when sharing a screen, and how to prepare foreigners' documentation for presentation during the transmission.

item.title: Labour inspectorate (PIP) checks after the 2026 changes and the employment of foreigners - residence card and work permit [COSC own material]
item.description:
From 8 July 2026 the National Labour Inspectorate (Panstwowa Inspekcja Pracy, PIP) may carry out an inspection or particular inspection activities remotely, request electronic documents and an online transmission, summon persons from outside the inspectorate's area, and - where an order to remove breaches has not been complied with - establish by administrative decision that an employment relationship exists (Act of 11 March 2026, Dz.U. 2026 poz. 473). We explain when a residence card (karta pobytu) alone is not enough to take up work, when a work permit is required, how documents must match the actual conditions of employment, and how to prepare the company for an inspection - based on 16 case studies.

item.title: Remote labour inspection - when the inspector does not come to the company [COSC own material]
item.description:
From 8 July 2026 the National Labour Inspectorate (Panstwowa Inspekcja Pracy, PIP) may carry out an inspection or particular inspection activities remotely - by post or by electronic means of communication (art. 26 ust. 5-8 of the Act on PIP as amended by the Act of 11 March 2026, Dz.U. 2026 poz. 473). The inspector may also require an online transmission allowing documents to be examined and persons to be heard and questioned (art. 23 ust. 1 pkt 2a). We discuss the conditions for such an inspection, how the identity card and authorisation are presented, data security requirements, and what changes for a company employing foreigners.

item.title: Remote labour inspection - the employer's duties step by step [COSC own material]
item.description:
From 8 July 2026 a labour inspector may carry out an inspection or particular activities remotely - by electronic means of communication or by a postal operator, without the employer's consent; the basis is the Act of 11 March 2026 (Dz.U. 2026 poz. 473). We set out the employer's duties at each stage: verifying the identity card and authorisation (art. 24 of the Act on PIP), producing personal files and documents (art. 23 ust. 1 pkt 5), the conditions for online transmission, data security, providing the conditions and means for the inspection (art. 27), the report and objections within 7 days (art. 31), and post-inspection measures - with a checklist and the documentation of lawful employment of foreigners.

item.title: Eight times fewer work visas — what the MSWiA data mean for foreigners and employers
item.description:
The Ministry of the Interior and Administration (MSWiA) reported 16,000 work visas issued in Q1 2026, against 123,000 in Q1 2022; 38,000 work permits against 122,000; and 2,700 enforced return decisions against about 900. We explain the rules behind the drop — the Act of 20 March 2025 (Dz.U. 2025 poz. 621), electronic-only applications through MOS (Moduł Obsługi Spraw, the case-handling module) from 27 April 2026 (art. 225a ust. 1 ustawy o cudzoziemcach) and the regulation Dz.U. 2026 poz. 1072 — and what follows from them in practice for a foreigner and for an employer. Own material of the Centre for Foreigners' Affairs Service (Centrum Obsługi Spraw Cudzoziemców).
Source: Centrum Obsługi Spraw Cudzoziemców (materiał własny) More & contact: https://cosc.org.pl/artykul-mniej-wiz-pracowniczych-dane-mswia-2026.html?lang=en&utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=aktualnosci-en • WhatsApp +48 539 999 549

item.title: Which residence application should you file? A router with fees and information on what goes through MOS and what stays on paper [COSC own material]
item.description:
A new router page on cosc.org.pl helps a foreigner choose the right type of residence permit application. For each category we give the amount of the stamp duty (from PLN 85 to PLN 640, plus PLN 100 for issuing the residence card - karta pobytu) and the way of filing: through the MOS (Modul Obslugi Spraw) portal or - in four cases, including intra-corporate transfer and family reunification where the foreigner is outside Poland - only in paper form. We also explain why filing an application in the wrong mode is among the most frequent reasons for refusal.

item.title: Temporary residence and work: the MOS application step by step, with deadlines and fees [COSC own material]
item.description:
Instructions for a foreigner who wants to file an application for a temporary residence and work permit in the MOS (Modul Obslugi Spraw) portal on their own. We describe six steps: preparing documents, setting up an account, the annex signed electronically by the employer (link valid for 30 days), completing the application, attachments (photo up to 2.5 MB, single file up to 10 MB, up to 50 MB in total) and the summons to appear in person. We give the fees: PLN 440 stamp duty and PLN 100 for issuing the residence card (karta pobytu), PLN 50 for a child under 16, a pupil and a student. We remind you that a draft application is kept for 45 days, that for supplementing formal deficiencies the authority sets a deadline of no less than 7 days, and that if the system is unavailable the application is filed within 3 working days after the failure is removed.
